spyglass: getting started
=========================

spyglass explores Minecraft: Java Edition seeds on your own computer: where
structures and biomes are, maps, and searches for the seeds that fit what you
want. It works for seeds and for your own world saves.

This folder holds three programs:

  spyglass           the command: locate, render, search, heights, world
  spyglass-viewer    the map app
  spyglass-extract   builds the game data spyglass needs, once per game version

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Mojang or Microsoft.


1. The first run on Windows and macOS
-------------------------------------

These programs aren't code-signed, so your system warns you the first time.

  Windows: if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose
  "More info", then "Run anyway".

  macOS: open Terminal in this folder and run

      xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .

  once. Otherwise macOS says the programs "can't be opened". You can also
  allow each one in System Settings > Privacy & Security > "Open Anyway".

To check that a download wasn't changed on the way, compare its SHA-256 with
the one in SHA256SUMS on the release page, or verify its provenance with the
GitHub CLI:

    gh attestation verify <archive> --repo farrcraft/spyglass


2. Get the game data
--------------------

spyglass ships nothing of Mojang's. The extractor downloads the game's server
jar from Mojang, checks it, and builds the data spyglass reads from it, all on
your machine:

    spyglass-extract 26.3

(`spyglass-extract` alone uses the latest release.) Run it once for each game
version you want.

It needs a Java runtime of the version the game needs: Java 25 for 26.3. If
you've played that version, you probably have one already. The extractor
looks in the official Minecraft Launcher and the Modrinth App, after
JAVA_HOME and PATH. Otherwise install one, for example Eclipse Temurin from
https://adoptium.net, or point the extractor at one with --java <path>.

The data goes in your per-user data folder:

    Windows  %LOCALAPPDATA%\spyglass\data\bundles
    macOS    ~/Library/Application Support/spyglass/bundles
    Linux    ~/.local/share/spyglass/bundles

Set SPYGLASS_BUNDLES to use another folder. Every program finds the data
there, wherever you run it from.


3. Use it
---------

    spyglass locate structure '#minecraft:village' --seed 12345
    spyglass locate structure minecraft:fortress --seed 12345 --dimension nether
    spyglass locate structure '#minecraft:village' --world "My World" --from player
    spyglass render --seed 12345 --structures '#minecraft:village' --spawn -o map.png
    spyglass search -q 'require 2 minecraft:swamp_hut within 600 of spawn' --time 60s

On Windows, in PowerShell or cmd, use double quotes instead of single quotes.

Every command has --help, and --json for scripts. Or start spyglass-viewer
for the map.

On Linux, the viewer needs the usual desktop libraries (on Debian and Ubuntu:
libxkbcommon0, libwayland-client0, libx11-6, libxcursor1, libxrandr2, libxi6
and libvulkan1). Most desktops already have them.


4. Which game versions
----------------------

`spyglass --version` lists the game versions this build was checked against
the real game for. Data for any other version still works, with a warning
that its answers may differ from the game's. A newer spyglass may support it.
